A consolidation release: one consistent CLI and installer experience
across Linux, Windows and macOS, a real (evidence-based, not assumed)
reliability fix, a measured, verified reduction in package size, and —
new for this release — real field validation of Windows and macOS
against actual ISP-level DPI on physical hardware. **The underlying
bypass engine — nftables/WinDivert/PF, DNS-over-HTTPS, TLS record
fragmentation, the decision ladder — is unchanged from v1.2.0-rc1**;
this release is about the product around it, not a rewrite of it.

## New: `dpictl`

The primary CLI on all three platforms, replacing `dpi-proxy-ctl`
(kept as a compatibility alias — existing scripts keep working
unchanged):

```
dpictl status               # short summary
dpictl status --verbose     # full detail (the old default)
dpictl doctor                # health checks, PASS/WARN/FAIL
dpictl diagnose discord.com  # DNS + HTTPS check for one site
dpictl support-bundle        # local diagnostics archive, redacted, no telemetry
dpictl logs | start | stop | restart | reload | version
```

- **`doctor`**: read-only checks for service health, the interception
  layer, DNS/DoH, internet reachability, that the binary actually
  supports transparent mode, other known DPI tools (dpi-bypass,
  GoodbyeDPI, zapret, SpoofDPI, ByeDPI, tpws, ciadpi) or a VPN
  interface that might interfere, and stale rules left over from a
  stopped service. Never disables anything it finds.
- **`support-bundle`**: a local `.tar.gz`/`.zip` with version, OS,
  status, logs, config and service state — redacted (tokens/keys/
  passwords, your home directory, your username, and your per-domain
  DNS decision history collapsed to a count, never the raw list). No
  telemetry: this only ever writes a local file.
- **Installer UX**: Windows and macOS now ship a double-clickable
  `Install`/`Uninstall` (`.cmd` with UAC self-elevation on Windows,
  `.command` for Terminal.app on macOS) alongside the existing
  `install.ps1`/`install.sh` for scripted/advanced use. Linux keeps its
  terminal `install.sh`.

Full reference: [docs/cli.md](../../docs/cli.md).

## Reliability: a real, evidence-based fix

Every scenario in "install once and forget about it" — Wi-Fi
reconnect, network switches, sleep/wake, service restart, crash
recovery, stale rule cleanup, boot before the network is up — was
audited against the actual source and existing tests, not assumed.
Almost all of it was already correctly implemented and already
regression-tested. The one real gap: on Linux, the network fingerprint
that scopes learned bypass decisions per-network could collide for two
different networks sharing a common gateway IP (192.168.1.1 and
phone-hotspot defaults are extremely common) when there was no SSID to
tell them apart — plain ethernet, or Wi-Fi without `nmcli` installed.
Windows and macOS already solved this by folding the gateway's MAC
into their fingerprint; Linux now does the same, reading the kernel's
own ARP table (no packet ever sent). Covered by a new regression test
proving two networks with the same gateway IP and different MACs no
longer collide.

## Smart engine: audited, no changes needed

Per-host and per-network decision learning, IPv4/IPv6-independent
decisions, decision expiry, cooldown after a failed bypass, avoiding
unnecessary probing, scoped QUIC/TCP fallback, no sibling-domain
inheritance, and manual `strategy.conf` rules always overriding
learned decisions — all independently verified against source and
existing tests. Nothing here needed changing; where the milestone
brief says "do not increase complexity unless measurable," this area
had nothing measurable to fix.

## Performance: measured, then reduced

Measured first, on real CI runners, not assumed: package size going
into this release was well above commonly assumed figures — 7.3 MB on
Windows and 5.2-6.0 MB on macOS (both static-link OpenSSL, by design,
so the shipped binary depends on nothing but the OS). Applied stripping
of packaged binaries (never the WinDivert driver files, shipped
unmodified) and link-time dead-code elimination:

| Platform | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Linux | 137,488 B | 113,312 B (-17.6%) |
| Windows | 7,646,856 B | 6,018,560 B (-21.3%) |
| macOS arm64 | 5,477,032 B | 4,296,184 B (-21.6%) |
| macOS x86_64 | 5,976,976 B | 4,781,152 B (-20.0%) |

Switching Windows/macOS to dynamic OpenSSL linking was considered and
rejected: it would shrink the binary further but reintroduce the
runtime-dependency fragility static linking was chosen to avoid.
Full breakdown and measured RAM/CPU/throughput: [docs/performance.md](../../docs/performance.md).

## Platform validation

> **Linux**: real ISP/DPI field-tested (unchanged from v1.2.0-rc1).
> **Windows (Beta)**: fully end-to-end tested on real Windows GitHub
> runners with the real WinDivert driver, and field-tested on a
> physical Windows PC against real ISP-level DPI (Turkey) —
> DPI-blocked sites (Discord and others) opened normally after a
> system-wide install, with no manual proxy or DNS configuration.
> **macOS (Beta)**: fully end-to-end tested on real macOS GitHub
> runners with real PF and launchd, and field-tested on a physical Mac
> against real ISP-level DPI (Turkey) — DPI-blocked sites opened
> normally with system-wide transparent mode, no manual configuration.

None of this branch's changes touch the interception/DoH/TLS
fragmentation engine itself — the field validation above confirms the
existing engine on this branch's product/CLI layer, on one physical
machine and network per platform. It is not yet validated across a
wide range of consumer hardware, networks or ISPs.

## Assets

- `dpi-proxy-linux-x86_64` — Linux binary (install from source with `scripts/install.sh`)
- `dpi-proxy-windows-x86_64.zip` — Windows transparent mode (Beta) + SOCKS5
- `dpi-proxy-macos-arm64.zip`, `dpi-proxy-macos-x86_64.zip` — macOS transparent mode (Beta)
- `SHA256SUMS`
